title: 组合对象与预制体 / appearance decomposition and reusable assemblies
text: 用户描述外观不等于指定实现方案。Appearance-first composite modeling: distinguish visible requirements from explicit implementation constraints. Decompose silhouette, independently colored faces, trim, articulated parts, interaction targets and repeated units before choosing primitives. One geometry with one material has one whole-object color; rounded-box controls the silhouette, not independent face colors. Build a root and child parts with parent-local transforms and separate materials. A thin rounded panel can be a rounded-box flattened along its local normal by Transform; keep its colored surface outside the body to avoid z-fighting. Inspect a representative assembly from several angles, exercise its actual transforms, then use prefab.manage capture and instantiate for repeats. Prefabs copy a subtree with fresh ids; they are snapshots, not live-linked definitions, and captured script string references are not automatically rebound. Configure each instance using returned ids. Examples: a die has a body plus face marks; a vehicle has a body plus rotating wheels; a cabinet has a body plus hinged doors; a colored puzzle piece has a dark body plus independently colored face tiles. A 3x3x3 cube may use 27 copies of a body-plus-six-tiles prefab, with interior tiles omitted or hidden per instance (54 exterior tiles). Bind tiles to their piece, not to fixed world faces. Do not duplicate the whole hierarchy with a single-mesh instance pool. Verify part counts, color roles, spacing, local orientation and child motion after rotation, save/reopen and Play. Author initial position/rotationDegrees/scale through entity.create transform or transform.set, and static appearance through component.configure/material.set. Do not attach initialization-only scripts to each repeated part. Reserve scripts for temporal state, input, rules and animation. Rotating a joint or puzzle layer requires a common pivot and transformed member positions as well as orientations; rotating each child around its own center is not a layer turn.

title: 圆角立方体 / rounded box geometry
text: For rounded cubes, beveled cubies and rounded blocks (圆角立方体、倒角方块), use entity.create or entity.create-many with kind rounded-box. This uses Engine createRoundedBox3D. radius defaults to 0.075 local units (0..0.5), segments defaults to 4 (1..16). Geometry is centered at the local origin with size 1 x 1 x 1 before Transform. Use uniform scale to preserve a circular corner radius. Use component.configure on haiyue.render.geometry to change kind, radius and segments; keep material configuration separate. PBR requires scene lighting. Never substitute ordinary cube for an explicit rounded-box requirement. Verify the rendered corners, including after save/reopen and in Play.

title: Camera framing and projection
text: Use a persisted gameplay camera as the shared authoring and Play authority. Inspect the current camera before editing it. Orthographic projection is appropriate when parallel board edges must remain parallel; perspective is appropriate when depth cues matter. A straight top-down 3D camera has 90 degrees elevation. camera.set orthographicSize is the full visible vertical world span; horizontal span also depends on aspect. Input conversion must still use engine picking rather than duplicating these projection formulas. Frame or follow an explicit target and verify the result with a Play screenshot.

title: Keyboard, pointer and touch input
text: Map keyboard and pointer input to named gameplay actions. A pressed action is a one-tick transition while held input remains active across ticks. pointerEvents() x/y are canvas-normalized 0..1 coordinates with top-left origin, x right and y down; they are neither world coordinates nor camera-local coordinates. For scene placement, configure haiyue.interaction.pointer on the target surface, enable down or click, and consume api.input.interactions() filtered by type and stable entityId. hit.point is world [x,y,z], including camera projection, aspect and pose. Convert it to the logical grid using the same origin, axes and spacing as rendering; transformed boards require world-to-board conversion. Never hardcode a screen-to-world multiplier or rebuild camera rays in game scripts. Meshes can occlude the target; configure decorative blockers as penetrable when appropriate. Define down, move, up, cancel and invalid gesture behavior. Verify center and corner hits after resize and camera movement, for both orthographic and perspective projections, using authoritative grid observations and rendered placement. Resolve stable project ids with api.read.find(id), not world.getEntity(id), which only recognizes runtime ids or names. Capture the gesture target on down and retain it until up/cancel even when the pointer leaves the mesh. For empty-background orbit, use a raw pointer down with no scene hit; do not require an invisible background mesh to be hit. Update the configured camera transform/control, not the objects. Treat missing entities and missing hits as diagnostic failures, not successful movements. With capturePointer enabled, drag/up/cancel retain the original target outside its mesh; point is the last valid world surface hit, not a new off-mesh intersection. Use pointerEvents() for the current normalized pointer displacement. Interaction events require configured hit surfaces: a visible mesh without haiyue.interaction.pointer can yield no interaction event, so an empty interactions() list alone does not prove empty background. Before interpreting misses as camera drags, inspect preview.validate pointerTargets and configure coverage for every intended selectable surface or a deliberate proxy. For a composite object, resolve a hit child to its logical owner; do not whitelist one sample entity id for all repeated pieces. Use the hit face normal and drag direction to select the intended axis/layer, and update logical coordinates after each completed turn. Camera orientation changes alone are not orbiting around a target; inspect and use the supported camera transform/control API.

title: Fixed-step simulation and physics
text: Gameplay simulation and physics advance on fixed ticks. Persist world settings, body and collider components before using runtime physics operations. Separate authoritative state from presentation. Validate movement, collision or trigger transitions with deterministic stepping, physics queries and gameplay observations rather than relying on elapsed wall time.

title: Play verification evidence
text: A successful preview start is not acceptance evidence. Exercise the authored gameplay trigger, step the fixed simulation, inspect authoritative gameplay state, capture the rendered frame and evaluate the task against persisted observations. Use the full observations bundle returned by play.capture: state and PNG are sampled together before asynchronous encoding. Do not combine an earlier inspect state with a later screenshot. Gameplay signals are under gameplay[index].value; read the actual payload before evaluating. Built-in performance has finite, tick, frame and timeMs, not fps. No current Play tool produces visual-analysis. Screenshot presence proves capture only, not visual correctness. Exercise real transforms as well as gameplay events. Keep stable trigger and observation identifiers so failures can be replayed and repaired. Prefer play.pointer-gesture for complete clicks/drags: points=[{"phase":"down","x":0.5,"y":0.5},{"phase":"move","x":0.65,"y":0.5},{"phase":"up","x":0.65,"y":0.5}], with optional settleTicks for animation. Coordinates are normalized and must be chosen from inspected targets, not assumed to hit every scene. The tool pauses, schedules and processes each event, and returns baseline/final evidence. For every interactive acceptance criterion, record a baseline with play.inspect, simulate down/move/up using the same pointerId with play.input at successive currentTick+1/+2/+3, then play.step(3) and inspect/capture again. play.input only schedules; a large future tick does not execute until stepping reaches it. Also test cancel and background gestures. Compare authoritative state.entities transforms and the camera, not only self-reported action counters; increment counters only after a real state change. A screenshot or an incremented counter cannot prove that an object rotated or the camera moved. On failure inspect hit targets, resolved entity ids and script errors before retrying. Tool projections may be truncated; projectionTruncated marks an abbreviated view and task.evaluate always reads the full persisted artifact. Signal array indices use dot notation, for example gameplay.0.value.metrics.moveCount. play.pointer-gesture steps report the observed interaction target and world hit, while effects report actual entity changes and camera changes. A null interactionTargetId means no configured interaction was observed, not proof of empty background. Do not repeat a gesture after a result-size error: it may already have executed; inspect current state first.

title: Presentation, effects and audio
text: Treat lighting, post-processing, particles, animation, HUD and audio as explicit versioned components. Add only supported component schemas from the registry, keep runtime ownership unambiguous, and verify structural state together with a screenshot or inspection artifact.
